messages:
ari: Draft PRD snapshot for Dedicated capacity commitments — need quick alignment on SLA targets, autoscale acceptance, and customer-driven constraints. Copy of acceptance criteria below. Please react with :eyes: if you can review by EOD.

ari: PRD excerpt:
```
SLA targets: p99 latency <= 300ms for 8-token gen; throughput per reserved GPU: 250 reqs/s; availability 99.95% monthly; burst pool available 25% above committed throughput for 5 minutes.
Autoscale behavior: scale-up within 30s when sustained 80% utilization for 60s; scale-down not below warm pool; cooldown 300s.
Fallback: automatic routing to smaller model variant when queue time > 500ms.
Acceptance tests: load test at 1.2x committed for 6 hours; graceful degrade test; warm-pool failover; billing attribution preserved.
Edge cases: long-tail seq length spikes; KV cache thrash; cold-start after maintenance; HSM failovers.
```

devon: A few questions: 1) p99 300ms is tight for some Llama2 variants on A100. Is that for 8-token only? 2) how do we measure 'queue time'? 3) warm pools = reserved-only or cross-tenant?

ari: Good Qs. Yes it's for short responses (<=16 tokens). Queue time = time request spends waiting in serving queue before dispatch. Warm pools should be customer-isolated for Dedicated by default; can opt into shared burst with consent.

leila: From infra POV, scale-up 30s is doable but depends on provisioning type. If Dedicated uses pre-warmed islands, we can meet <30s. If cold-provision from cloud, need 180-300s. Recommend specify 'fast-path' (prewarmed) and 'cold-path' with different SLOs.

sam_sre: For acceptance tests, add 'canary failure + traffic shift' test and SLA degradation alerting (pager at 99.9% degrade). Also include runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-sla

jonah_cs: Customer ask: enterprise A wants guaranteed 500rps for a slot during business hours. Need clear escalation SLA and compensation terms in PRD.

ari: Noted — I'll add cadence for business hours window and on-call escalation. For compensation terms, legal will draft, but we need measurable metric and window.

devon: Edge-case: quantized models might have different p99; add model-profile mapping to PRD so runtime selects variant with matching SLO.

leila: Also call out KV-cache warmup time per model; add a 2-minute expected KV warmup in spec.

ari: Updated acceptance criteria snippet — please review:
```
Acceptance criteria (final):
- p99 latency <= 300ms for <=16 tokens for models in 'gold' profile on prewarmed infra
- Throughput: reserved pool sustain at committed RPS for 1h without queue growth
- Burst: 25% above commit for min 5m with correct billing
- Autoscale: fast-path scale-up triggered when CPU/GPU util >80% + queue growth for 60s; scale-up latency <= 60s on fast-path
- Fallback routing to compatible model if per-request estimated latency > threshold
- Tests: 1. 1.2x load soak for 6h 2. failover test 3. canary rollout 4. billing sanity
```

ari: tagging @devon @leila @sam_sre @jonah_cs — can you reply with :+1: or any blockers by EOD? If no blockers, I'll mark PRD ready for RFC next week.

deploy-bot: New doc created: /prod/prds/dedicated-commitments/205567-draft.md

devon: +1 but we should relax 300ms to 400ms for some heavy-attention models, conditioned on model-profile. I'll DM with mapping.

leila: +1 from infra with note: add 'cold-path' recovery SLO 5min.

sam_sre: +1, add alert thresholds to doc.

jonah_cs: +1, will coordinate with enterprise A for business hours SLA window.

ari: Great — I'll integrate updates and push RFC. Thanks all :rocket:
